findings.citation: Two guards around the plan-save flow (M6.2): (1) **conflict detection**: if the plan file is touched by an open PR from an `agent:go`-assigned issue, block the save and surface the conflict;
findings.description: The oracle and conflict checks establish conflict from two independent facts (any agent:go issue and any plan-edit PR); they never establish that the PR is from the labeled issue, so unrelated issue/PR pairs are reported as conflicts despite the goal's association requirement.

findings.citation: Treat a PR as touching the plan file exactly when its head branch is a plan-edit branch, i.e. was named by the plan-save flow's convention (see `plan-save.ts`). Document this gap in the module.
findings.description: The branch behavior is checked, but no check verifies that the changed-files approximation and its limitation are documented.

findings.citation: Do not edit any other file. Strict TS, no `any`. Sibling modules may be imported only with `import type`; at runtime only Node built-ins are available (the modules run under Node 24 with built-in type stripping).
findings.description: The scenario verifier executes transpile-stripped modules but performs no static TypeScript/import inspection, so `any`, non-type sibling imports, and failure to satisfy the declared strict typings can pass.
Every queue scenario injects both `fs` and `queueDir`; no check exercises or observes the default directory expansion.

findings.citation: plus the `FsLike` interface (Node `fs/promises` subset, the default):
findings.description: All queue checks inject FakeFs and runtime imports cannot observe a TypeScript interface, so neither the exported FsLike contract nor the default fs/promises implementation is verified.

findings.citation: A file that cannot be read or parsed counts as `failed` with an error message and is skipped.
findings.description: `replaySkipsCorrupt` covers JSON parse failure only; no scenario makes readFile fail for a listed entry. Checks also inspect only the errors array length, not that it contains a meaningful string message.
`enqueueFailurePropagates` exercises only writeFile failure; mkdir and rename failure propagation are not checked.

publicationScope: Admission judgments and native outcome metadata only; prompts, raw streams, HTTP bodies, configuration and credential state excluded.
